text:
raj: Heads-up — after rolling nvidia-container-toolkit 1.10.0 -> 1.11.0 on eu-west GPU nodes we started seeing image runtime failures, short lived but affecting ~15% of jobs
ciara: saw this too on a couple of pods. error in container logs: "error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
sam: do we have the `nvidia-container-runtime` host bind mounted? previous fixes were rshared bind propagation issues
natalie: yes, host path is mounted, but note the toolkit image change also updated symlink layout under /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 -> now some containers expect different SONAMEs
raj: repro steps i used: `docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint bash nvidia/cuda:12.2-base -c "nvidia-smi"` inside failing host -> crashes with same lib not found
miguel: can you paste `ls -l /run/nvidia/` and `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ | grep -i nvidia` from host?
raj: from host: ```
$ ls -l /run/nvidia/
crw-rw---- 1 root root 195,   0 Mar  6 12:10 nvidiactl
crw-rw---- 1 root root 195, 255 Mar  6 12:10 nvidia-uvm
$ ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ | grep nvidia
lrwxrwxrwx  1 root root    14 Mar  6 11:59 libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.525.105.17
-rw-r--r--  1 root root  1024 Mar  6 11:59 libnvidia-ml.so.1
```
ciara: interesting — libcuda symlink exists on host but inside container the path is missing. sounds like bind propagation or uid/gid remapping on our immutable base image
sam: quick mitigation: pin toolkit to 1.10.0 and restart kubelets on a canary pool. we should also add an init-container that verifies /usr/lib*/libcuda*.
raj: tried pinning, reduced failures to near-zero in canary eu-west-2, but us-central still shows occasional flakes after rolling there
miguel: could this be kernel module mismatch? some hosts updated kernel on same day as toolkit -> module versioning mismatch means nvidia pods can't load libcuda? check `modinfo nvidia`
natalie: also saw some pods failing with `nvidia-uvm: Unknown symbol` in dmesg earlier — that points to mismatched driver/kernel combo
natalie: planning: 1) pause toolkit rollout, 2) roll back nodes that got kernel updates, 3) add a preflight check job during node upgrade that runs `docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi`
raj: agree. also we need to add a kubelet-level mount test to block nodes that present rprivate propagation; some of our custom hostPath wrappers accidentally set propagation to rprivate during image build
ciara: action item: eng-runtime to add a simple readiness hook to the GPU device plugin that validates library visibility. if it fails, mark node unschedulable and alert infra-team
sam: note on capacity/cost: draining nodes for rollback will take ~8-10 hours for a full region — we should prioritize affected AZs only. cost estimate: ~0.6 GPU-hours lost per pod eviction at current queue sizes
miguel: i can scope a small script to detect host symlink vs container visibility and run it as a DaemonSet. will open PR after standup
raj: created incident ticket INC-2026 and linked the canary logs. tagging @miguel for the daemonset PR, @natalie for kernel rollback plan
deploy-bot: [deployment] rollback to toolkit 1.10.0 initiated on cluster eu-west (runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-toolkit-rollback) :rotating_light:
ciara: thanks. also let's add a short blurb to runbook about `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` heuristics and fallback to host bind mounts. we should avoid hacks but have clear emergency steps
raj: final note — add a metric to alert on `container_logs =~ /libcuda.so.*cannot open/` so SRE sees it before user tickets spike
ciara: agreed. i'll draft the alert and the runbook update after lunch :coffee:
sam: ping if you need help with canary rollback automation, i can help coordinate capacity shifts
miguel: starting a small daemonset PoC now, will post logs and PR link in this thread
raj: closing the loop — marking this thread for follow-ups, will update INC-2026 when rollback completes.
